seg_membrane_response — EMPROOF response op

• Data kinds: image2d → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.seg_membrane_response(image, sigma: 'float' = 1.5, normalize: 'bool' = True) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import emproof; emproof.seg_membrane_response(image, sigma: 'float' = 1.5, normalize: 'bool' = True) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsemproof.get("seg_membrane_response"))

Usage

Response [0, ∞) to the dark lines (cell membranes) of an EM section. From the eigenvalues λ1 ≥ λ2 of the Gaussian-smoothed Hessian, max(λ1 − |λ2|, 0) (the closed form of Steger's line detection, scale-normalized by σ²).

On a dark line the 2nd-order derivative across it is large and positive (λ1) and along it 0 (λ2), so λ1 − |λ2| rises. Dark clumps (mitochondrial interiors, synaptic vesicles) have λ1 ≈ λ2 > 0, which cancel out to near 0 -- only membranes are picked up. normalize=True sets the 99.5 percentile of the section to 1 (the thresholds of seg_* are written on that scale). If scikit-image is available, the registry's sk_frangi (fs.apply(img, "sk_frangi", a=0.5, b=0.5)) can also fill the same slot (the prototype measured AUC with that one).

Parameters

image : (H, W) float

Raw EM (bright = cytoplasm, dark = membrane). Any range (only gradient ratios are looked at).

sigma : float

Smoothing σ [px]. About half the membrane thickness (1.5-2.5 for CREMI at 4 nm/px).
